sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 16:59

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 16:59:1
items.html:
Quantity and a measure of a receiving place, but only in the discernment of the quality of the light itself etc. One must not err here whatsoever regarding an imaginary place; rather, quality means the number of the disparities of form in the degree, without the distinction of the merit and importance in it. And this is what he answered: it is true that the smallest degree in the upper one is greater than everything beneath it, yet this is only a qualitative distinction and not a quantitative distinction. For example, the Malchut in the upper one is greater than all the worlds and Sefirot beneath her; even so, it is impossible even for two Sefirot beneath her to be found in the Malchut of the upper one, for in terms of quantity there is only one form in the Malchut of the upper one, which is why she is regarded as only one Sefira. Therefore she cannot receive into her two Sefirot that have two forms separate from one another, which necessarily require two separate places: for the Sefira is the discernment of the light, and the place is the discernment of the vessel ascribed to it.
Therefore the four Sefirot of Yetzira cannot be found in the place of one Sefira of the Malchut of Atzilut; rather, they need four Sefirot of the Malchut of Atzilut, for each Sefira needs a place of its own, since every disparity of form in the light necessitates a disparity of form in the place as well, which is the vessel.
